notes: This suite exists because the logistic-only schedule-free result was a single-model conclusion.
Seed-7 numbers are a regression baseline. The verdict is in runs/schedule-free-verified/mlp/seed-sweep-summary.md.

The ten-seed result on this model REVERSES the logistic one: schedule-free AdamW beats the tuned cosine in 9/10 seeds here (logistic: it lost 10/10), while a constant learning rate still beats schedule-free in 9/10 seeds. So the direction of 'schedule-free vs tuned schedule' is model-dependent; what is stable across both models is that the constant rate wins.

trial[schedule_free_adamw].test_loss carries its own tolerance (loss_abs = 0.005) because that arm alone amplifies last-bit libm differences between platforms; every other expectation in this file stays at loss_abs = 1e-6. Basis, measured rather than tuned: (a) the same suite run under Linux in python:3.12-slim differs from the Windows pin by up to 2.0e-4 across the twelve suites that pin this arm (this file: see the numbers in REPRODUCTION.md 5.17); (b) nudging math.exp/sqrt/tanh/erf by one ULP on a single machine moves this arm by up to 9.8e-4 (scripts/perturbation_probe.py), while every other arm in the same suites moves by exactly 0. The tolerance is 5x the largest movement observed by either method. Compensating checks this file keeps exact: the arm epochs_to_target pin (an integer, stable across platforms and in the ULP probe), its test_accuracy pin, and the schedule-free negative control, which must still detect a broken averaging step.
